result.title: Motion Conditioned World Modeling for Embodied Visual Tracking
result.summary: World models support embodied decision-making by predicting future environment states. In embodied visual tracking, uncertain target motion and robot-induced viewpoint changes jointly affect visual observations, making future-state prediction challenging. We propose Motion-Conditioned World Modeling, which incorporates predicted target-motion distributions and robot ego-motion into latent state transitions. A Geometry--Progress module jointly models geometric paths and single-step travel distances through shared motion modes and path-conditioned progress distributions. This formulation captures uncertainty in route selection and motion progress while preserving their dependence. Action-induced coordinate transformations express predicted paths in the next robot frame, providing geometrically grounded conditions for future visual-state prediction. Future visual feature reconstruction supervises the motion predictor through the conditioned transition branch, linking explicit motion representations to subsequent observations. The model is jointly optimized with motion likelihood, feature reconstruction, and expert-action supervision, enabling the tracking policy to combine visual context with predictive motion cues.Experiments on three embodied tracking benchmarks demonstrate improved tracking performance and cross-environment generalization with a lightweight $0.5$B backbone.

AI.brief_summary: 提出运动条件化的世界模型：将对目标运动分布的预测与机器人自运动注入 latent 状态转移，用几何—进度模块联合建模路径与单步位移，并以未来视觉特征重建、运动似然和专家动作联合训练跟踪策略。
AI.relevance_reason: 其不确定性条件化的 latent 转移与「以未来视觉特征重建监督运动预测」的做法，可能可供核查 LVR 中预测状态更新、视觉证据保留与训练信号分配，但任务为具身跟踪策略，与多模态推理的联系较间接。
